subject: history_social
passage: Derawar Fort rises from the flat sands of the Cholistan Desert in Punjab, Pakistan. Its forty round bastions and walls some thirty meters high can be seen from many kilometers away. Today the land around the fort is sparsely settled and receives very little rain. Yet the fort stands beside the dry bed of the Hakra, a river that flowed through Cholistan thousands of years ago, and archaeologists have recorded the remains of hundreds of ancient settlements strung along that same riverbed. These remains suggest that ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: the Hakra still carries water underground during the rainy season.
choices.B: the region once supported far more people than it does today.
choices.C: Derawar Fort was built by the people who lived in the ancient settlements.
choices.D: the ancient settlements were abandoned because the fort was built.

explanation.why: The land is nearly empty now, but hundreds of ancient settlements once lined the riverbed when the Hakra flowed. Many settlements mean many people, so the region must once have been much more heavily populated than it is today.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text calls the riverbed dry and says nothing about underground water or a rainy season.
explanation.B: Correct. Hundreds of settlements along a river that once flowed point to a large past population in an area that is now sparsely settled.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text does not say who built the fort, and the settlements date from thousands of years ago.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Nothing in the text links the fort to the settlements' abandonment; the settlements are far older.
